dedupe_keys.name: gis b me semi synthetic benchmark for elevator maintenance scheduling on real urban road networks

description: GIS-B-ME is a semi-synthetic benchmark for scheduling preventive maintenance of lifts (elevators) in buildings, built on real urban building locations and directed road networks in selected areas of Beijing, Shanghai and Chongqing. It was published on Zenodo on 20 September 2026 (version 1.0) by Xuesong Xu, Junjie He and colleagues of Zhejiang University of Technology, with the Huzhou Special Equipment Inspection Center and Xizi Elevator Technology. Version 1.0 holds 135 instances across three cities, three task scales, three spatial patterns and five random seeds, with 72,000 task records, plus road-distance and travel-time matrices, frozen geographic inputs, generation settings, validation outputs and independently validated best-known feasible schedules. Coverage: study areas in three Chinese cities. Access: a ZIP of about 541 MB with checksum and citation files on Zenodo, mirrored as a GitHub release. Licence: ODbL 1.0 for database content, CC BY 4.0 for documentation and MIT for scripts; OpenStreetMap-derived content keeps OSM attribution. Free. Caveats: tasks, building types and service attributes are generated and do not represent real lift registries. Simulation uses: testing technician routing and maintenance scheduling for building equipment. Related records: the OfficeGraph benchmark.
